_name: probe-2026-10-03-r4-dev-routing - the routing smoke after round 4 is pushed to dev
_why: About 12 questions on what round 4 touched directly: the three kept REST uses, an SOP list on the graph, catalog counts, a how-to first turn, caller identity, a follow-up that stays NS, a CC work request and a lab named like an entity. Roughly 12 turns, one cheap pass per login, PAID: needs the operator's go. Dev only.
_instance_warning: Dev's numbers differ from production's. The two assay-kind numbers (75 with samples, 8 without) are dev's, measured for the 3 Oct review; re-pin them with pin_probe_truths.py on any other box. Every other expected value is a per-box check named in _by_box, not a number.
_run: Run the file twice on the same box, once per login (cli --user/--password): cases tagged login:both on each login, login:member only on the NON-ADMIN login. Judge a case only on the login its tag names. Fill the FILL markers first (each is listed in _fill; replace every occurrence in a COPY with sed), keep the filled copy out of git: it holds real ids.

_fill.LAB_IS_ENTITY: a lab name from the lab catalog that is ALSO an investigation title or alias (or a project) on this box
_fill.SOP_TITLE: any SOP title the login can see: the protocol_title of a DERIVED_FROM edge, or SELECT title FROM seek_production.sops LIMIT 1 for an admin
_fill.UID_IN_LOGIN_PROJECT: a sample UID inside one of the LOGIN's projects (run once per login): MATCH (s:Sample) WHERE <login project id> IN s.project_ids RETURN s.uuid LIMIT 1

_by_box: Numbers not pinned in a criterion are checked per box and login on the day from the same source the case's _why names (a REST row count, the box's context json, a scoped Cypher). Never copy a number from another box.

cypher: MATCH (a:Assay) WHERE EXISTS { (a)-[:INPUT_TO|OUTPUT_OF]-(:Sample) } RETURN count(a) AS n
MATCH (a:Assay) WHERE NOT EXISTS { (a)-[:INPUT_TO|OUTPUT_OF]-(:Sample) } RETURN count(a) AS n

retrieval_path_selection.description: Which execution path inside the NExtSEEK engine a question takes.

variants.name: Downloading a named SOP is the kept REST use
variants._why: REST is for finding people, downloading SOPs and retrieving samples by UID. The title is filled per box.

turns.label: main
turns.query: Give me the file for the SOP titled __FILL:SOP_TITLE__

sample_retrieve.description: Pull the full record for samples the user can already name.

variants.name: Retrieval by a named UID is the kept REST use
variants._why: The UID is a sample inside the login's own projects, chosen per box (see _fill). total_samples from the endpoint is the per-box truth.

turns.label: main
turns.query: Pull up the full record for __FILL:UID_IN_LOGIN_PROJECT__

graph_traversal.description: Questions that follow the graph's structure: which study, investigation or project samples belong to and counts scoped to them, which samples went into or came out of an assay (Assay nodes joined by INPUT_TO and OUTPUT_OF), which protocols samples used, and which studies, projects or assays hold something.

variants.name: Assay kinds with samples and with none come from the Assay EXISTS
variants._why: A how-many over a catalog kind with a has/lacks predicate goes to the graph, never a REST list preview.

turns.label: main
turns.query: How many assay kinds have samples, and how many have none?

project_summary_report.description: The reporter's project view: a formal NIH, RPPR, annual or progress report, upload statistics over a time window, published sample counts, and the SOPs registered to a project. An open-ended summary of a whole project or investigation goes to Container-CC, and a plain count or breakdown is a graph question.

variants.name: A lab named like an investigation scopes the report to it
variants._why: U4.1. Per box: the lab name used must be a lab AND an investigation, project or alias there (see _fill). Footer says 'both a lab and the investigation (or project)'.

turns.label: main
turns.query: Progress report for the __FILL:LAB_IS_ENTITY__ group in 2025

pass_criteria.value: (?is)\A(?!.*(is not the name of a project))
